_comment: Main Street: the Cruise screen is set here, and the diner is on it (diner.json). street.kn5 and ground.bin are written
by tools/DinerScene (build_street.py: compose_street.py in Blender, then prepare_prop.py and DinerSceneBuilder; see
docs/screens/diner.md). One model for every light of the day, with a sky dome for each (STREET_SKY_DAY, _DUSK, _NIGHT).
Los Angeles, late 1960s. Positions are metres, x along Main Street and z across it: the origin is the middle of Main
Street in front of the diner, which stands on the north-east corner (towards -z) of the crossing with a cross street
at x = -36. Main Street is 12 m kerb to kerb: a parking lane each side (z -6 to -3 and 3 to 6) and a lane each way
between them. Headings are degrees about the vertical, 0 facing +z, -90 facing west (-x).
player: where the player's car is parked, in the parking lane on the diner's side east of its lot, facing west.
laneOffset, rivalStop, approachFrom, leaveTo: the rivals' lane, as streets' are (a rival comes up the lane to the
player's left from behind, stops alongside and goes on out of sight).
sun: the key light's direction by day, towards the sun. lights: the renderer's light for each light of the day (see
docs/modding.md, streets); lamps are lit at night at x, y, z (under the cobra heads, under the diner's overhang, the
pylon's neon). glow: how bright each self-lit material glows at a light of the day (0 to 4): the diner's signs and
coloured glass, the pylon's neon, the motel's star sign, the billboard; the materials are named as in
compose_street.py's Blender scene (a Sketchfab model's after its id). model: the one model for every light.
